strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with effective visualization (Figure 2) demonstrating VLM misalignment with robotic signals
Practical and lightweight method design that seamlessly integrates with existing VLA pipelines without additional VLM forward passes

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (RoboCasa-Kitchen, LIBERO) with diverse settings (fine-tuning, from-scratch, real-world) and consistent improvements (e.g., +11.2% on pick-and-place, +13.3% real-world)
Thorough ablation studies examining soft label targets, augmentation strategies, and quantitative alignment metrics (CKNNA)
Strong real-world validation including generalization tests (visual, physical, language grounding)
Excellent presentation with clear writing, informative visualizations, and comprehensive reproducibility documentation (implementation details, hyperparameters, public datasets)
Effectiveness across multiple VLM backbones and data regimes demonstrates robustness
Outperforms alternative VLM training strategies (RoboBrain, VeBrain, Cosmos-Reason1)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: weighted contrastive learning and view cutoff augmentation are straightforward applications of existing techniques (Khosla et al. 2020; Shen et al. 2020) with the main contribution being a natural choice of weights based on proprioceptive distances

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: CKNNA alignment metric improvements are somewhat circular since the loss explicitly optimizes for this; missing ablations on temperature parameter β sensitivity and analysis of what specific robotic signals the learned representations capture

Narrow scope of proprioceptive information: limited to end-effector position, 6D rotation, and gripper state; unclear scalability to high-DoF systems (humanoids, dexterous hands) or applicability beyond manipulation tasks
Modest improvements on LIBERO benchmark (0.7% absolute gain on average; 95.7% → 96.4%) suggest potential ceiling effects and task-dependent benefits rather than general applicability
Batch size dependency acknowledged in Appendix D.1 (LIBERO batch 32 vs. RoboCasa 64) reduces generalizability and requires careful hyperparameter tuning

Real-world experiments limited in scale (60 demonstrations, 24 trials, no confidence intervals or statistical significance testing) and show inconsistent improvements across metrics (e.g., close-lid partial success bars)

Missing ablations on sensitivity to hyperparameters (temperature τ=0.2, β=1.0) and justification for cosine decay schedule for λ; unclear why proprioceptive distance outperforms next-action distance as soft labels (Table 3a shows alternatives underperform but lacks explanation)

From-scratch experiments show extremely low baseline performance on weaker backbones (2.0-4.0% accuracy), making improvements harder to interpret and potentially reflecting scaling effects rather than method benefit
Generalizability concerns: exclusively evaluated on manipulation with similar action spaces; applicability to locomotion, navigation, or different morphologies untested
Limited analysis of failure cases and when RS-CL doesn't provide benefits; view cutoff contribution orthogonal to main contribution and not clearly separated
